item.title: Tigers look for parting shot at Guardians in finale of season series
item.description: The high point of the Detroit Tigers' season came against the Cleveland Guardians on Aug. 13, when they moved into a share of an American League wild-card spot with a home win.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The high point of the Detroit Tigers' season came against the Cleveland Guardians on Aug. 13, when they moved into a share of an American League wild-card spot with a home win. Their low point did, as well, as Cleveland's two walk-off wins in a doubleheader sweep Friday essentially knocked the Tigers out of the postseason hunt. Detroit gets its final shot at the Guardians this year on Sunday afternoon, when the teams wrap up a four-game series in Cleveland. Tigers right-hander Jackson Jobe (1-2, 4.63 ERA) will get the start against Guardians righty Gavin Williams (13-7, 3.81). Three-time All-Star Riley Greene gave the visitors a bit of payback on Saturday, amassing a career-high tying four hits, four RBIs, three runs and two homers in leading Detroit to a 6-0 rout of Cleveland. It was the ninth multi-homer game of his five-year career and his first blasts anywhere since spending 20 days on the injured list with a strained right hamstring. Greene's seven home runs in Cleveland are his most in any visiting ballpark. "We come here all the time, so maybe that's the reason why," Greene said, laughing. "It's baseball. It happens. After what happened last night, you just have to flush it and get to the next day." The Guardians (72-71) are now even with the Toronto Blue Jays in the battle for the final AL wild-card position, but Cleveland loses the head-to-head tiebreaker. Detroit (65-77) is 6 1/2 games behind them with 20 to play. Greene had been 1-for-13 since being activated, but came to life against his offseason buddy, Guardians All-Star pitcher Parker Messick. The homers totaled 828 feet and each landed atop the high wall in left-center field. "I think he owes me a fishing trip that we've been talking about the last few times I've seen him," Messick quipped. "To go backside, left-center field is just a really good swing. I throw those balls there to a lot of other lefties and don't get that same result." There won't be any hard feelings the next time they hang out in Florida, though. Greene said it didn't matter who he was hitting against, he was desperate to get back in a groove. "I just had to get good pitches to hit and was trying to get on strikes," Greene said. "On the first one, I was just trying to find barrels and make something happen." Jobe has either been terrific or terrible in five starts, all coming since Aug. 8 as the Tigers have fallen apart. Three of them have seen him allow one or fewer runs, but he was rocked for 10 earned runs in 8 2/3 combined innings during the other two. His only career game against the Guardians was a home loss on May 23, 2025, when he gave up two runs in five innings. Greene's big night coincided with Framber Valdez and two relievers tossing a three-hitter. Angel Martinez, David Fry and Angel Genao each had a single as Cleveland was shut out for the 15th time, tied for the most in the majors with the Cincinnati Reds and Pittsburgh Pirates. "That's the most four-seam (fastballs Valdez has) used, almost 20%," Guardians manager Stephen Vogt said. "That's not something he historically does. The two fastballs, and he threw just enough off-speed, to keep us off of that." Williams last pitched on Sept. 1, holding Toronto without an earned run in seven innings of a 6-1 victory. It was one of four wins by Cleveland in nine games on its homestand that ends Sunday. Nicknamed "The Big Rig," Williams has not faced Detroit this season. He is 3-2 with a 1.88 ERA in seven career starts against the Central Division rival. "We capitalized (Friday) night, right? Then today, we got beat by a very good pitcher," Vogt said. "That was the story, and we'll be ready Sunday." --Field Level Media

item.title: Irán abordará problemas económicos y advierte de que los nuevos ataques serán "más dolorosos"
item.description: Irán ha afirmado que intensificará sus esfuerzos para hacer frente a los problemas provocados por las sanciones estadounidenses que están paralizando su economía, mientras que un alto cargo iraní ha advertido de una "respuesta dolorosa" si el país sufre nuevos ataques.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Irán ha afirmado que intensificará sus esfuerzos para hacer frente a los problemas provocados por las sanciones estadounidenses que están paralizando su economía, mientras que un alto cargo iraní ha advertido de una "respuesta dolorosa" si el país sufre nuevos ataques. Seis meses después de los ataques de Estados Unidos e Israel contra Irán, la guerra parece estar en un punto muerto. El acuerdo preliminar de alto el fuego alcanzado en junio se ha desmoronado y se han logrado pocos avances en los esfuerzos diplomáticos para volver a encarrilar el proceso de paz. Tras una pausa en las acciones militares durante gran parte de julio, se han reanudado los ataques de represalia: el Mando Central de Estados Unidos ha afirmado que el sábado atacó tres petroleros iraníes en respuesta al lanzamiento de misiles balísticos por parte del Cuerpo de la Guardia Revolucionaria Islámica de Irán contra dos buques de la Armada de Estados Unidos. Tras los ataques, el presidente del Parlamento iraní, Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf, declaró el domingo que Estados Unidos debería comprender que las reglas del juego en la guerra contra Irán han cambiado "antes de que sea demasiado tarde". "A partir de ahora, cualquier ataque contra los intereses y la seguridad de Irán recibirá una respuesta más rápida, más contundente y más dolorosa", afirmó en un discurso publicado en su canal de Telegram. Teherán ha demostrado que sigue conservando la capacidad de atacar los intereses estadounidenses en los países vecinos y de bloquear el flujo de petróleo a través del estrecho de Ormuz, por donde circulaba una quinta parte del suministro mundial de petróleo antes del conflicto. SANCIONES Y EL BLOQUEO PETROLÍFERO ASFIXIAN LA ECONOMÍA Sin embargo, la campaña de Estados Unidos para estrangular la economía iraní mediante el bloqueo de sus exportaciones de petróleo y la lucha contra la elusión de sanciones resulta cada vez más difícil de soportar, según han afirmado tres fuentes iraníes de alto rango. En su discurso del domingo, Qalibaf añadió que, junto al frente militar, la principal batalla de Irán se libraba ahora en torno a la producción y los medios de subsistencia de la población. Mencionó las fuertes fluctuaciones monetarias, la inflación, el desempleo y la gestión del mercado como retos principales, y añadió que los iraníes podían tolerar las penurias, pero no la mala gestión ni la inacción, y esperaban que el Gobierno actuara con rapidez. El ministro de Economía de Irán, Ali Madanizadeh, afirmó que Teherán tenía previsto responder a la presión económica de Estados Unidos con reformas y rechazó la idea de que las sanciones le hicieran cambiar de rumbo, según informaron el domingo los medios estatales. "Hablan de presión económica y aislamiento, de romper los lazos financieros, y creen que, al ejercer presión sobre la economía de un país, pueden cambiar las decisiones de su pueblo", afirmó Madanizadeh. "Tengo que aclarar un punto: la responsabilidad de reformar la economía de Irán recae en su Gobierno y su pueblo, no en el Tesoro de Estados Unidos". Por otra parte, el viceministro de Economía, Morteza Zamanian, declaró el domingo que el "Cuartel General de la Guerra Económica" del ministerio estaba redoblando sus esfuerzos para resolver los problemas causados por la guerra, según la agencia de noticias semioficial Tasnim. ISLA DE KHARG HA SUFRIDO 550 ATAQUES EN LOS ÚLTIMOS MESES, SEGÚN IRÁN Irán es el tercer mayor productor de la Organización de Países Exportadores de Petróleo y, antes de la guerra, exportaba el 90 % de su crudo a través de su centro de exportación de la isla de Kharg. Los flujos se han visto interrumpidos desde que, a mediados de abril, comenzó el bloqueo estadounidense a las exportaciones de petróleo iraní. El 31 de agosto, Trump publicó un mensaje de una sola línea en las redes sociales acompañado de un vídeo generado por IA en el que se veía cómo la isla de Kharg "volaba en mil pedazos". Las autoridades iraníes han prometido una respuesta contundente si Kharg es atacada. En una entrevista emitida el domingo en la televisión estatal, el ministro de Petróleo de Irán, Mohsen Paknejad, afirmó que la isla había sido alcanzada unas 550 veces en los meses anteriores, pero que seguía en funcionamiento. Irán también ha impuesto un bloqueo en el estrecho de Ormuz, lo que supone un problema para el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, al provocar un aumento de los precios del combustible a nivel mundial de cara a las elecciones de mitad de mandato de su Partido Republicano en noviembre. El sábado, el Mando Central de Estados Unidos afirmó que había atacado tres buques iraníes, incluido uno frente a la costa de la isla de Kharg, después de que el Cuerpo de la Guardia Revolucionaria Islámica de Irán lanzara misiles balísticos contra dos buques de la Armada de Estados Unidos. "Que el mensaje al IRGC quede claro: si disparan contra dos de nuestros buques, os impondremos un coste económico aún mayor: derribaremos tres de los vuestros", afirmó el almirante Brad Cooper, jefe del Mando Central de Estados Unidos, que supervisa las fuerzas armadas estadounidenses en Oriente Medio.

item.title: Ukraine-Les Américains Witkoff et Kushner à Kyiv après Moscou
item.description: Les émissaires américains Steve Witkoff et Jared Kushner ont rencontré dimanche à Kyiv le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky au lendemain d'un entretien de trois heures à Moscou avec le président russe Vladimir Poutine, dans le cadre d'une nouvelle tentative des Etats-Unis de mettre fin à quatre ans et demi de guerre entre l'Ukraine et la Russie.
item.dc:creator: Max Hunder, Anna Voitenko
item.content:encoded: Les émissaires américains Steve Witkoff et Jared Kushner ont rencontré dimanche à Kyiv le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky au lendemain d'un entretien de trois heures à Moscou avec le président russe Vladimir Poutine, dans le cadre d'une nouvelle tentative des Etats-Unis de mettre fin à quatre ans et demi de guerre entre l'Ukraine et la Russie. Le président américain Donald Trump, qui avait affirmé avant son retour à la Maison blanche en 2024 qu'il trouverait rapidement une issue au conflit, a laissé entendre vendredi que Washington avait une nouvelle proposition à soumettre à ces deux pays, sans plus de précisions. Ses précédentes initiatives n'ont débouché sur aucune avancée significative et ses représentants semblent une nouvelle fois ne guère avoir progressé lors de leur rencontre samedi avec Vladimir Poutine. Ce dernier a néanmoins qualifié cet entretien de "fortement utile" et un responsable de la Maison blanche a dit à Reuters que de nouvelles annonces seraient faites dans les prochaines semaines. Avant sa rencontre avec Steve Witkoff et Jared Kushner en compagnie d'autres responsables ukrainiens de haut rang dans le centre de Kyiv, Volodimir Zelensky a dit sur les réseaux sociaux la volonté de l'Ukraine de mettre fin à la guerre. "Des garanties de sécurité sont nécessaires. Une paix digne après la guerre est nécessaire. Nous avons formulé des propositions", a déclaré le président ukrainien. Volodimir Zelensky considère que l'implication des Etats-Unis est indispensable à tout accord. Il pense qu'il existe une fenêtre d'opportunité pour conclure une paix avec la Russie avant que la classe politique américaine ne bascule bientôt vers la prochaine élection présidentielle de 2028 aux Etats-Unis. Une source informée de cette présence a déclaré à Reuters que des représentants de la France, de la Grande-Bretagne et de l'Allemagne pour les questions de sécurité nationale se trouvaient dimanche à Kyiv. Cette source n'a pas précisé à quels entretiens participeraient ces émissaires européens. ESPOIRS Steve Witkoff et Jared Kushner se sont déjà rendus à plusieurs reprises à Moscou en tant que médiateurs mais il s'agit de leur première visite à Kyiv. Cette venue nourrit les espoirs de certains habitants de la capitale ukrainienne, bombardée sans relâche par la Russie depuis plusieurs semaines. "Le problème peut être réglé en un clin d'oeil. Nous voulons la paix. J'ai moi-même combattu donc je sais ce qu'est la guerre. Nous avons besoin de la paix car il n'y a pas d'autre issue", dit Stepan Yermak, un ancien combattant. Svitlana Kurylenko, serveuse dans un café, espère pour sa part "un accord qui ne sera jamais rompu". "Qu'on laisse l'Ukraine tranquille et son peuple vivre en paix", dit cette jeune femme de 19 ans. Russes et Ukrainiens affichent cependant des positions impossibles à réconcilier en l'état, aussi bien sur le plan territorial avec des revendications de Moscou sur des régions ukrainiennes que Kyiv refuse de céder, que sur l'avenir même de l'Ukraine et ses volontés de rapprochement avec l'Union européenne et l'Otan. Si le front des combats évolue peu au sol, la Russie et l'Ukraine ont intensifié leurs frappes aériennes dans la profondeur depuis plusieurs semaines. La Russie a néanmoins annoncé une pause de ses bombardements sur Kyiv jusqu'à lundi et Volodimir Zelensky a déclaré que l'Ukraine s'abstiendrait également de viser Moscou sur cette période. L'armée russe a tout de même poursuivi sa campagne de bombardements sur d'autres villes ukrainiennes samedi tandis que les forces ukrainiennes ont déclaré dimanche avoir frappé au cours de la nuit une raffinerie à Riazan, à près de 500 km de la frontière.

item.title: Pirates' Paul Skenes faces childhood favorite Angels in series finale
item.description: Paul Skenes has started two All-Star Games, won an ERA title and garnered the 2025 National League Cy Young Award. But one thing the hard-throwing right-hander hasn't done in his career is pitch against the team he rooted for while growing up in southern California.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Paul Skenes has started two All-Star Games, won an ERA title and garnered the 2025 National League Cy Young Award. But one thing the hard-throwing right-hander hasn't done in his career is pitch against the team he rooted for while growing up in southern California. That will change Sunday afternoon when Skenes (9-11, 3.97 ERA) takes the mound for the Pittsburgh Pirates (70-73) when they host the Los Angeles Angels (54-88) in the rubber game of their three-game series. Skenes starred for El Toro High School in Lake Forest, Calif., about a 25-minute drive south of Angel Stadium. It's the same high school that produced a pair of pretty talented major league third basemen named Nolan Arenado and Matt Chapman. Skenes brings a seven-start winless streak into the contest after picking up a no-decision in his last start on Tuesday against San Francisco. He left after allowing five runs, including a three-run homer by Rafael Devers, on eight hits over 4 2/3 innings. He walked three, struck out four and departed with a six-run lead after throwing 95 pitches, 56 for strikes. "I feel good. I think I could have gone longer," Skenes said afterward. "I don't know how many pitches I threw today, but I know they're trying to watch volume a little bit, so I'm not pushing back too much." Skenes' last win came on July 19 in a 7-1 victory at Cleveland. Pittsburgh, trying to capture its fourth straight series, needs a win to keep its slim National League playoff hopes alive. The Pirates are five games out of the final wild-card spot with only 19 games remaining. Right-hander Walbert Urena (9-9, 2.85 ERA), expected to receive some down-ballot votes for A.L. Rookie of the Year, gets the start for Los Angeles. Urena, who has yielded just a .203 batting average in 23 starts, comes in off arguably the best start of his career in a 10-1 victory over the New York Yankees. He allowed one run on five hits in seven innings with no walks and tied his career high with eight strikeouts. "No panic when you watch him," Angels manager Kurt Suzuki said of the 22-year-old Urena. "When you face the Yankees and the Phillies and the Red Sox and teams like that, there's always a little bit of a sense of anxiety and when you watch Walby from pitch one, it was zero anxiety. I think it was (11 straight strikes to start the game). That's the sign of an ace. I thought he pitched great tonight." Los Angeles, trying to avoid the first 100-loss season in franchise history, bounced back from a 1-0 loss in Friday's series opener to defeat the Pirates, 6-1, on Saturday. Yusei Kikuchi allowed five hits over six innings and struck out six en route to his first victory since Sept. 24, 2025 against Kansas City. Josh Lowe homered, Wade Meckler had a pair of doubles and two RBIs and Zach Neto went 3-for-5 with an RBI and a run scored to lead the Angels. Los Angeles got a bit of a scare when Mike Trout, who went 2-for-4 with a run scored and an RBI, was hit on the left hand by a Yohan Ramirez sweeper in the ninth inning and was lifted for pinch-runner Jose Siri. Trout underwent X-rays after the game, which came back negative. -Field Level Media

item.title: Orioles eager to halt 'frustrating' stretch in finale vs. Red Sox
item.description: The Baltimore Orioles need to generate offense to have any chance to win games, and that's even more clear after the past two outings.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Baltimore Orioles need to generate offense to have any chance to win games, and that's even more clear after the past two outings. They've failed to score in a pair of consecutive shutout defeats to the visiting Boston Red Sox. The Red Sox (78-65) will vie for a four-game series sweep of the Orioles on Sunday afternoon. "They're making pitches, and to their credit," Orioles first baseman Pete Alonso said. "But also for us, I don't think we're necessarily capitalizing the most when we get pitches in the zone. It's really frustrating for sure." The Orioles (69-74) will look to shed a five-game skid. "We've been here before, and for our guys it's just regrouping, trusting each other, playing for each other," Baltimore manager Craig Albernaz said. "Passing the baton. That's when we're at our best, when we're playing that team approach, nine versus one against the starter." After having Saturday night off, former Orioles catcher Adley Rutschman figures to be back behind the plate for Boston. He homered twice in the series opener in a much-anticipated return to Baltimore. Until that offensive outburst against the Orioles, Rutschman's biggest contributions and much of his focus had been on the defensive side. He said he knows that's important going forward as well. "Making sure that everything's running smoothly from the catching side, and that's kind of been the biggest thing as far as workload goes," Rutschman said. "Making sure I'm doing those guys a good service when I'm behind the plate." Boston's starters haven't allowed a run in back-to-back games. "Second night in a row we've got the starter out there through seven innings," Red Sox manager Chad Tracy said following Saturday night's 5-0 victory. Boston has named left-hander Payton Tolle (8-6, 3.23 ERA) as its starter for Sunday's game. He's 4-0 in his last 10 starts, though he's without a decision in his past three outings. Tolle has given the Red Sox at least five innings in eight consecutive starts, beginning July 20 when he allowed four runs in 5 2/3 innings to the Orioles in a no-decision -- though a game Boston won. The Red Sox also won June 3 at home when Tolle blanked the Orioles for six innings. Those are the only times Tolle has faced Baltimore in two big-league seasons. Right-hander Kyle Bradish (7-12, 4.01) will be the starting pitcher for the Orioles. He has gone seven consecutive starts without a victory, posting a 0-3 mark during that stretch. His last victory came when he held the Red Sox to one run in six innings July 22 in Boston, though he took the loss during an April meeting at home versus the Red Sox. In 11 career starts against the Red Sox, he's 2-6 with a 6.12 ERA. Much might be asked of Bradish and any other Baltimore pitchers if the Orioles can't crank up some offense. "Seems like our guys are offensively pressing a little bit, trying to do too much," Albernaz said. "Not everyone and it's not every single at-bat. It's just, you just see they're trying, they know where we're at. They're trying to come through for the team and come through for the rest of the boys, and sometimes it works out where they put together some good swings." --Field Level Media

item.title: Iran to tackle economic issues, says further attacks will be 'more painful'
item.description: The U.S. campaign to throttle Iran's economy by blockading its oil exports and stopping sanctions evasion is growing increasingly difficult to withstand, three senior Iranian sources said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Iran said it will step up efforts to tackle problems created by the U.S. sanctions that are crippling its economy, while a senior Iranian official warned of a "painful response" if it comes under further attack. Six months after U.S.-Israeli strikes against Iran, the war appears to be at a stalemate. A preliminary ceasefire accord reached in June has unravelled and little progress has been made in diplomatic efforts to get the peace process back on track. After a pause in military action for much of July, tit-for-tat strikes have resumed with U.S. Central Command saying it hit three [USN:L1N44Y028 TEXT:"Iranian tankers"] on Saturday in response to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps launching ballistic missiles at two U.S. Navy ships. Following the attacks, Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf said on Sunday that the U.S. should understand that the rules of the game in the war against Iran have changed "before it is too late". "From now on, any attack against Iran’s interests and security will receive a faster, heavier and more painful response,” he said in a speech published on his Telegram channel. Tehran has shown it still retains the capability to attack U.S. interests in neighbouring countries and to shut down oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of global oil supplies flowed prior to the conflict. SANCTIONS, OIL BLOCKADE SQUEEZE ECONOMY However, the U.S. campaign to throttle Iran's economy by blockading its oil exports and stopping sanctions evasion is growing increasingly [USN:L1N44W081 TEXT:"difficult to withstand"], three senior Iranian sources have said. In his speech on Sunday, Qalibaf added that alongside the military front, Iran’s main battle was now over production and people’s livelihoods. He cited sharp currency fluctuations, inflation, unemployment and market management as major challenges, adding Iranians could tolerate hardship but not mismanagement or inaction and expected the government to act quickly. Iran's Economy Minister Ali Madanizadeh said that Tehran planned to respond to U.S. economic pressure with reforms and rejected the idea that sanctions would cause it to change course, according to state media on Sunday. “They speak of economic pressure and isolation, of breaking off financial ties and they think that by pressuring the economy of a country they can change the decisions of its people,” Madanizadeh said. “I have to clarify one point: the responsibility of reforming Iran’s economy is with its government and people, not with the U.S. Treasury." Separately, Economy Ministry deputy Morteza Zamanian said on Sunday that the ministry's “Economic War Headquarters” was doubling down on its work to resolve problems caused by the war, according to the semi-official Tasnim news agency. KHARG ISLAND HIT 550 TIMES IN PRIOR MONTHS, IRAN SAYS Iran is the third-largest producer in the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and exported 90% of its crude via its [USN:L1N44S09M TEXT:"Kharg Island"] export hub before the war. Flows have been disrupted since a U.S. blockade of Iranian oil exports began in mid-April. On August 31, Trump issued a one-line social media post accompanied by an AI-generated video depicting Kharg Island being "blown to smithereens." Iranian authorities have vowed a strong response if Kharg is attacked. In an interview aired on state TV on Sunday, Iran's Oil Minister Mohsen Paknejad said the island had been hit around 550 times in previous months but continued to operate. Iran has also imposed a blockade on the Strait of Hormuz, creating an issue for U.S. President Donald Trump by pushing up fuel prices globally ahead of midterm elections for his Republican Party in November. On Saturday, U.S. Central Command said it struck three Iranian vessels, including one off the coast of Kharg Island, after Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps launched ballistic missiles at two U.S. Navy ships. “Let the message to the IRGC be clear: If you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost — taking out three of yours," said Admiral Brad Cooper, head of U.S. Central Command, which oversees the U.S. military in the Middle East. The IRGC responded by threatening intensified strikes against U.S. military vessels in the region, and said later it targeted the three tankers as well as three U.S.-linked vessels in other areas. "Do not be deceived by the 'terrorist' U.S. military and refrain from any suspicious movement aimed at passing through unauthorized waterways," the IRGC Navy said in a statement carried on Iranian state TV. "Otherwise, you will be targeted." Tasnim, the semi-official Iranian news agency, had reported that four U.S. missiles hit a tanker in the area of Kharg's anchorage. Tasnim quoted local sources as saying there were no casualties and the tanker's crew was being evacuated. No American personnel were harmed, Central Command said. On Sunday, Tasnim reported that the IRGC had shot down a U.S. surveillance balloon over Erbil in northern Iraq, describing it as part of a broader effort to eliminate U.S. aerial surveillance and early-warning systems in the region.

item.title: Tyler Mahle, Braves look to slow down Phillies
item.description: Tyler Mahle has experienced a tale of two seasons, both individually and from a team standpoint.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Tyler Mahle has experienced a tale of two seasons, both individually and from a team standpoint. The veteran right-hander looks to continue his pleasant turnaround Sunday afternoon when the Atlanta Braves visit the Philadelphia Phillies in the third contest of a four-game set. After bouncing around in recent years, Mahle (5-10, 4.25 ERA) hoped to find a home when he signed with the San Francisco Giants over the winter. But he struggled to the tune of a 3-9 mark with a 5.13 ERA, prompting the team to trade him to Atlanta on Aug. 2. Mahle has become a vastly different pitcher in his time with the Braves, posting a 2-1 record with a 1.48 ERA in five starts. In his last start one week ago, he allowed one run in 6 2/3 innings against the Colorado Rockies, finishing with nine strikeouts and zero walks. "This is probably the best team I've ever been a part of," Mahle said, reflecting on his move from the scuffling Giants to the first-place Braves. "It's nice to know I could come in and hit the ground running and not miss a beat with where this team was already. I could just fit in and do my part." Mahle faced the Phillies twice in April while pitching for the Giants. He held Philadelphia scoreless over 5 2/3 innings in the first matchup before surrendering five runs in five innings later in the month. For his career, Mahle is 1-2 with a 3.80 ERA against the Phillies. Philadelphia will counter with Aaron Nola (6-10, 4.93), who also has been an improved pitcher of late. He has allowed one run or fewer in three of his last four starts, notching three wins during that stretch. In his last outing, Nola yielded one run in five innings against the Arizona Diamondbacks. "I notice that when I don't have that much life on the fastball, they foul more pitches off and run the pitch count up, and work better (at-bats)," Nola said after requiring 104 pitches to get 15 outs. Nola is 17-12 with a 3.80 ERA in 39 lifetime starts against Atlanta. The Braves won Friday's series opener 5-2 before the Phillies bounced back Saturday with a 4-2 triumph. Zack Wheeler gave Philadelphia six strong innings on Saturday, while Kyle Schwarber's MLB-leading 41st homer was the offensive highlight for the hosts. The Phillies (80-62) trail the Braves (84-58) by four games in the NL East. The teams have two games remaining in this series - Sunday and Monday - before meeting again for a three-game set next weekend in Atlanta. "We're close to them, and every game matters, especially against them," Wheeler said. "It can swing pretty quick. We know where we're at and we know where they're at, and where we're trying to be. So every game matters, especially against these guys." The Braves, who had won nine of their previous 11 games, managed only five hits in Saturday's setback. Ronald Acuna Jr. and Austin Riley belted solo homers in a losing effort. "You know when you've got him on the ropes, you've got to get something," Braves manager Walt Weiss said of the missed opportunities against Wheeler. "We didn't." --Field Level Media

item.title: Russia's Lavrov calls accusations of Moscow's involvement in Leipzig drone incident 'start of real war', TASS reports
item.description: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said on Sunday that the accusations levelled at Moscow by the West that it was involved in the drone incident at Germany's Leipzig airport were, "by and large, the start of a real war," state news agency TASS reported.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said on Sunday that the accusations levelled at Moscow by the West that it was involved in the drone incident at Germany's Leipzig airport were, "by and large, the start of a real war," state news agency TASS reported. "All these statements by Merz about making Germany the leading military power in Europe once again – they are being put into practice. He is, in effect, declaring war on us," Lavrov said, referring to German Chancellor Friedrich Merz. The German government [USN:L8N44T1P2 TEXT:"said on September 1"] that it had concluded that Russia was responsible for an attempted drone attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport last month and ordered a series of measures in response, including the closure of a consulate and a Russian cultural centre in Berlin. Russia [USN:L8N44U1IM TEXT:"dismissed"] the German accusations as baseless, accusing Berlin of planting evidence to frame Russia for the attack.

item.title: Greek PM rules out snap elections after unveiling tax cuts, wage hikes
item.description: Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis ruled out snap elections on Sunday a day after announcing a string of tax cuts and wage hikes, as he seeks to recover lost ground in opinion polls ahead of a general election due next year.
item.dc:creator: Lefteris Papadimas
item.content:encoded: Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis ruled out snap elections on Sunday a day after announcing a string of tax cuts and wage hikes, as he seeks to recover lost ground in opinion polls ahead of a general election due next year. His centre-right government, which was re-elected with 40.5% of the vote in 2023 promising to increase incomes, remains ahead in opinion polls but support has slipped to below 30% amid a protracted cost-of-living crisis [USN:L1N40K0PK TEXT:"and allegations of corruption."] "Elections will be held in spring 2027," he said during a press briefing on Sunday, dismissing media speculation about snap elections this year. He added that he believed his party could still secure an outright majority and win a third consecutive four-year term. On Saturday, Mitsotakis announced income [USN:L6N44X05V TEXT:"tax breaks and wage hikes"] worth €3.5 billion ($4.06 billion), equivalent to 1.5% of GDP, to be rolled out over the next four years. He also pledged to cut unemployment to 6% and reduce public debt to below 110% of GDP by 2030. The measures include an annual bonus of €400 for pensioners and €500 for public servants, a zero tax rate on annual incomes of up to €20,000 for farmers and families with three children, and a gradual reduction in advance tax payments for the self-employed and businesses to 50%. After a financial crisis in 2009 that triggered fears Greece would crash out of the euro zone, the country is now one of the best-performing in Europe. Greece's economy is expanding at an annual rate of 2%, outpacing the euro zone average. It expects a primary surplus of about 4% this year, double what was initially expected, giving fiscal space to fund the new measures.

item.title: Behind Kyle Harrison, Brewers chase series win vs. Reds
item.description: Kyle Harrison will try to bounce back from a disastrous start when the Milwaukee Brewers visit the Cincinnati Reds on Sunday afternoon in the decisive contest of the three-game series.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Kyle Harrison will try to bounce back from a disastrous start when the Milwaukee Brewers visit the Cincinnati Reds on Sunday afternoon in the decisive contest of the three-game series. Harrison (10-4, 3.45 ERA) allowed nine runs on 10 hits -- including five homers -- in 3 2/3 innings in a 17-3 romp by the Chicago Cubs on Monday. Most of the damage came against the left-hander's fastball, and the question was raised whether he may have been tipping his pitches. "Part of it's on me. I can't be giving away pitches in the first inning," Harrison said after that game. "When you know what's coming, it's a little bit easier to hit, I think. It's on me during the week. I knew these guys were looking for any kind of edge that they can get." Harrison has not been successful against Cincinnati during his career, going 0-1 with a 5.40 ERA in three games. His last start versus the Reds came when he was a member of the San Francisco Giants on Aug. 3, 2024. The long ball also led to Harrison's undoing in that contest, as he gave up four homers. Overall, he surrendered six runs and six hits in 3 2/3 innings with a walk and four strikeouts. Right-hander Brady Singer (5-13, 4.83), Cincinnati's scheduled starter for Sunday, also was ineffective in his most recent outing. Singer allowed four runs on 10 hits in 4 2/3 innings in a 5-0 loss to the San Diego Padres on Monday. "They put a lot of hits together," Singer said. "I tried to stay in the zone. Didn't want to start looking to chase and start walking guys. ... Tried to stay in the zone, left a lot of balls (over the middle of the plate)." Singer permitted only two hits and struck out seven batters over seven scoreless innings in a no-decision against Milwaukee on June 22. He is 2-2 with a 3.51 ERA in five career encounters (all starts) versus the Brewers. The Reds evened the series with a 5-3 win on Saturday night in a contest that featured a near-2 1/2-hour rain delay. Matt McLain homered to lead off the seventh inning and Cincinnati (68-74) added an insurance run in the eighth when Eugenio Suarez was able to score from second on a wild pitch. Elly De La Cruz and Tyler Stephenson also went deep for the National League Central cellar-dwelling Reds. Tony Santillan got the win despite allowing a run in his only inning. Emilio Pagan picked up his 21st save after loading the bases with one out in the ninth. He induced Luis Lara to pop up and William Contreras to fly out to end the game. Contreras homered for Milwaukee (88-55), which has lost four of seven games to see its lead over second-place Chicago trimmed to seven games in the NL Central. --Field Level Media

item.title: US envoys make first Kyiv visit amid Ukraine war peace push
item.description: The U.S. envoys arrived from Moscow where they held three hours of talks with Vladimir Putin, but did not appear to secure a breakthrough in the conflict.
item.dc:creator: Max Hunder, Anna Voitenko
item.content:encoded: U.S. peace envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy in Kyiv on Sunday as the Trump administration renewed its push to end Russia's four-and-a-half-year war in Ukraine . Kushner and Witkoff travelled from Moscow, where they [USN:L1N44X01Y TEXT:"held three hours of talks"] with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Saturday but did not appear to secure a breakthrough in the conflict. Previous rounds of U.S.-mediated peace talks encouraged by President Donald Trump , who campaigned on a promise to quickly end the war, have yielded few results. He [USN:L1N44W0SY TEXT:"suggested"] on Friday that the U.S. had a fresh proposal though he did not elaborate. Putin described Saturday's meeting as "highly useful", while a White House official told Reuters that next steps would be announced in the coming weeks. The two envoys met Zelenskiy and other top Ukrainian officials in central Kyiv. Zelenskiy, who believes Washington will be key to any peace deal, has said a window of opportunity to make peace exists before the U.S. begins focusing on its next presidential elections next summer. In a post on social media before the envoys' arrival, Zelenskiy said he had held a preparatory meeting with his negotiating team and said Ukraine wanted an end to the war. "Security guarantees are needed. A dignified post-war peace is needed. Our proposals have been drawn up," he said. A source familiar with the matter told Reuters the British, French and German national security advisers were also in Kyiv on Sunday. The source did not specify which meetings they would participate in. CAUTIOUS OPTIMISM ON THE STREETS OF KYIV Witkoff and Kushner, Trump's son-in-law, have visited Moscow several times in their roles as peace envoys. But Sunday will be their first visit to Kyiv in their capacity as U.S. negotiators. Their visit has long been sought by Ukraine's leadership, and on the streets of Kyiv, which has been bombarded heavily in recent weeks, some residents were hopeful. "The issue can be solved in the blink of an eye. We want peace. I've fought myself, so I know what war is like. We need peace, because there's no other way," said military veteran Stepan Yermak. In previous talks, the sides have remained far apart on a range of key issues, including the future of the eastern Ukrainian region of Donbas. Russia has demanded Ukraine's withdrawal from an entrenched belt of towns that it still controls there, but Kyiv has refused, reasoning that it can still hold on there for years. For Ukraine, hard security guarantees from its European allies and the U.S. are crucial to deterring Russia from invading again. "We need an agreement that will never be broken," said Svitlana Kurylenko, a 19-year-old cafe worker. "Just leave Ukraine alone and let people live in peace." TEMPORARY HALT IN STRIKES Though the front lines of the ground war remain largely static, both Russian and Ukrainian forces have intensified long-range air strikes in recent weeks. Russia has pounded the Ukrainian capital day and night with missiles and drones for the past two weeks, including an [USN:L1N44W0FE TEXT:"attack on Friday"] on the headquarters of the SBU security service. The Kremlin has said it would pause strikes on Kyiv until Monday, while Zelenskiy has said Ukraine would also halt strikes on Moscow. There was no let-up in fighting along the 1,200-km (750-mile) front, however, and Russia bombarded other Ukrainian cities on Saturday. Ukraine has inflicted damaging hits throughout the summer on Russian refineries, oil terminals and the warehouses of online retailer Wildberries, in an attempt to raise the cost to Moscow of continuing the war. Ukraine said on Sunday it had struck the Ryazan oil refinery, around 480 km (300 miles) inside Russia, overnight, causing a fire.

item.title: UK business minister to meet Jaguar Land Rover CEO over job cuts
item.description: Britain's business minister Jonathan Reynolds said he will meet Jaguar Land Rover's CEO this week to discuss job cuts at the country's biggest carmaker, amid reports it is looking to shed 4,000 roles.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Britain's business minister Jonathan Reynolds said he will meet Jaguar Land Rover's CEO this week to discuss job cuts at the country's biggest carmaker, amid reports it is looking to shed 4,000 roles. Reynolds told the BBC on Sunday that while he wanted to mitigate job losses, the business environment for carmakers was "challenging" in the UK and across Europe. "If this is about making sure over time that workforce is right to make the business as competitive as possible, that's the conversation we need to have," Reynolds said on Sunday. JLR, which employs about 30,000 people in Britain and whose largest plant is in Solihull, West Midlands, is owned by India's Tata Motors (TAMO.NS) . It said in a statement it needed to make £1.7 billion of savings over the next two years and as such it would be opening a voluntary redundancy programme. TARIFFS AND CHINESE IMPORTS "We need to adapt to evolving global market conditions," a JLR spokesperson said. The job cuts would be a setback for Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who took office six weeks ago, and has repeatedly said he wants to "reindustrialise" Britain. JLR, which also has major sites in central and northern England, has been affected by the fallout from tariffs imposed by U.S. President Donald Trump, as the U.S. is an important market for its luxury Range Rover and Defender models, while competition from Chinese models such as the Jaecoo 7 — ranked third among Britain's top-selling cars — is also hitting sales. The Times newspaper said 4,000 roles at JLR would be cut over two years through a redundancy programme due to be announced on Monday. Earlier in September, German carmaker Volkswagen's supervisory board [USN:L4N44V1K1 TEXT:"approved"] a transformation plan that will include cutting 50,000 jobs in its attempt to counter tariffs and Chinese competition.

item.title: China to pump $54 billion into state banks, insurers in capital-boosting push
item.description: Beijing is making the coordinated push to shore up capital across its financial system as weak loan demand remains a drag on the world's second-largest economy.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: China's finance ministry will inject a combined $54 billion into state-owned insurers and banks, the companies said on Sunday, in a coordinated push by Beijing to shore up capital across its financial system. China Life Insurance (Group) Co, the country's largest life insurer, will receive 35 billion yuan ($5.2 billion), while China Taiping Insurance Group will get 7 billion yuan, the two groups said in statements. Separately People's Insurance Company (Group) of China (601319.SS) said it planned to raise up to 15 billion yuan through a private placement of A-shares to the Ministry of Finance, with the proceeds to be used to replenish its capital. The initiative could help bolster state insurers that were directed to [USN:P8N3NE00R TEXT:"support the stock market"] with medium- and long-term funds, while positioning them to help regulators manage smaller, higher-risk insurance companies. FINANCIAL SECTOR STABILITY The insurance sector has been grappling with eroding profitability due to persistently low interest rates, with numerous small and mid-sized insurers reporting deteriorating solvency ratios. China Export and Credit Insurance Corp also said the finance ministry will inject 10 billion yuan to boost its core capital, and China Reinsurance (Group) said it will raise 3 billion yuan. "The injection is an important step by the country to enhance the financial sector's ability to serve the real economy and promote the high-quality development of the financial and insurance industries," China Life said in its statement, adding that it would strengthen the group's ability to withstand risks. Taiping said the funds would bolster its solvency and other key indicators. BANKS TAP RECAPITALISATION PLAN Separately, three state lenders on Sunday also announced they will receive a combined 290 billion yuan in capital injections. The plan was first [USN:L4N3ZS0O1 TEXT:"unveiled"] at an annual parliamentary meeting in March this year, extending a financing tool that had helped bolster some other big state banks [USN:L3N3QE05W TEXT:"last year"]. Agricultural Bank of China (601288.SS) and Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (601398.SS) , two of the country's largest state banks, said they planned to raise up to 160 billion yuan and 100 billion yuan respectively through private A-share placements to the finance ministry, China National Tobacco Corp and its subsidiaries. Both lenders said the proceeds would be used entirely to replenish core Tier 1 capital, in a move to help sustain credit expansion as Beijing leans on state banks to support growth. [USN:L4N443089 TEXT:"Weak loan demand"] remains a persistent drag on the world's second-largest economy, which also has been eroding profitability of the banking sector. The Export-Import Bank of China, one of the country's three policy lenders, said the finance ministry will inject 30 billion yuan into the bank, effectively enhancing its capital base. ($1 = 6.7108 Chinese yuan renminbi)

item.title: Quatre morts dans des frappes israéliennes au Sud-Liban
item.description: Quatre personnes, dont deux femmes, ont été tuées dimanche dans des frappes de l'armée israélienne dans le sud du Liban, a annoncé le ministère libanais de la Santé.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Quatre personnes, dont deux femmes, ont été tuées dimanche dans des frappes de l'armée israélienne dans le sud du Liban, a annoncé le ministère libanais de la Santé. L'armée israélienne a présenté ces frappes comme des représailles à des attaques de drones du Hezbollah dans des secteurs qu'elle occupe dans le Sud-Liban. Malgré un cessez-le-feu annoncé en juin sous la médiation des Etats-Unis, l'armée israélienne reste déployée dans ce qu'elle considère comme une zone de sécurité dans le sud du Liban. Le ministère libanais de la Santé a déclaré que deux hommes avaient été tués dans une localité située à la lisière de cette zone occupée par les forces israéliennes et que deux femmes avaient aussi péri à Arab Salim, qui se trouve bien plus au nord de cette zone. L'armée israélienne avait auparavant émis un ordre d'évacuation couvrant des secteurs proches d'un immeuble à Arab Salim, qu'elle entendait bombarder en raison de son utilisation par le Hezbollah, selon elle. Deux fillettes figurent parmi les six personnes blessées dans cette frappe. Le Hezbollah, mouvement chiite armé, rejette les négociations directes engagées par le gouvernement libanais avec Israël sous la médiation des Etats-Unis.

item.title: Moscow not ruling out trilateral meeting of Russian, US and Chinese leaders, agencies report
item.description: Russia's Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov said on Sunday that Moscow has not ruled out a trilateral meeting between the presidents of Russia, the U.S. and China, state news agency TASS reported.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russia's Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov said on Sunday that Moscow has not ruled out a trilateral meeting between the presidents of Russia, the U.S. and China, state news agency TASS reported. However, before moving on to the actual preparations, it is necessary to understand what the meeting's agenda would be, Ryabkov said. "Here, the main question boils down to how the substance of the meeting will be formulated, and what we can expect as a result." Earlier this month, Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov [USN:L1N44T0U1 TEXT:"raised the possibility"] of Vladimir Putin, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping meeting at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China, in November. On Sunday, Ushakov was quoted by Russian news agencies as saying that while such a meeting of Russian, U.S. and Chinese leaders "would not be without merit," its organisation was the prerogative of the summit's hosts. "If they are able to organise such a meeting – and this requires a certain amount of diplomatic preparation – then I think it could take place," Ushakov said. The Kremlin also plans to set up bilateral meetings for Putin during the summit, including one with Xi Jinping, and, "if the opportunity arises," a meeting with Trump, Ushakov said.

item.title: Avalanche hits glacier on China's Muztagh Ata in Xinjiang, state media says
item.description: An avalanche struck Glacier No. 2 on Muztagh Ata, near China's border with Tajikistan in the northwestern Xinjiang region, with several tourists capturing footage on their phones, state broadcaster CCTV reported on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: An avalanche struck Glacier No. 2 on Muztagh Ata, near China's border with Tajikistan in the northwestern Xinjiang region, with several tourists capturing footage on their phones, state broadcaster CCTV reported on Sunday. Video showed a massive wall of snow and ice cascading down the mountainside, forming a snow cloud more than 100 metres (328 feet) wide, the broadcaster said. There were no casualties or property damage because the avalanche took place in an unpopulated area far from major roads, CCTV reported. The main peak of Muztagh Ata, covered by ice and glaciers, is 7,546 metres high. Glacier No. 2 is closed to the public because of heightened risks of glacial activity. The local culture and tourism bureau on Saturday warned tourists not to enter unauthorised high-risk restricted zones on Muztagh Ata, citing complex terrain, volatile weather, weak communication signals and extremely poor rescue conditions.

item.title: OPEC+ keeps oil output policy unchanged for October
item.description: OPEC+ kept its oil output policy unchanged for October at a meeting on Sunday, it said in a statement, as the producer group needs to agree new quotas before deciding its next output steps.
item.dc:creator: Ahmad Ghaddar, Olesya Astakhova, Alex Lawler
item.content:encoded: OPEC+ kept its oil output policy unchanged for October at a meeting on Sunday, it said in a statement, as the producer group needs to agree new quotas before deciding its next output steps. The meeting of seven core OPEC+ members — Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan and Oman — comes as the Iran war continues to disrupt oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz, limiting [USN:L6N44D030 TEXT:"OPEC+'s influence"] over prices and market share. In August, OPEC+ agreed its production boost for September, completing a phased rollback of a 1.65 million-barrel-per-day supply cut first agreed in 2023. Despite the agreed production increases, the group made up of the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and its allies, including Russia, still produces far below its targets because of the war. OPEC'S POWER LIMITED BY IRAN CONFLICT "OPEC+ currently has very limited power over the physical oil market," said Jorge Leon of Rystad Energy. "The group can change production targets on paper, but it cannot guarantee that those barrels will be produced or actually reach the market." "The focus now shifts away from monthly production adjustments and towards the much more consequential debate over 2027." OPEC+ still has another layer of production cuts in place, covering most members of the 21-country group until the end of 2026. Before the group decides how to unwind the cuts and return production to the market, it needs to review members' oil production capacity to set 2027 output baselines, which form the basis for quotas. This debate will likely happen later in 2026 and hence OPEC+ is likely to [USN:L6N43U0TI TEXT:"pause its output increases"] for the fourth quarter, sources earlier told Reuters. The statement on Sunday made no mention of policy beyond October. Only the seven OPEC+ members who met on Sunday, plus the United Arab Emirates until it left OPEC in May, have been involved in monthly output decisions in recent years. The seven countries will hold their next meeting on October 4.

item.title: At flood-destroyed China-Nepal border, no sign of a once-busy port
item.description: About 20 Chinese rescue workers in bright orange operated excavators, shovels and ground-penetrating radar detectors on Sunday in an effort to find hundreds of people missing since a tsunami-like mudslide destroyed China’s main border crossing with Nepal.
item.dc:creator: Nicoco Chan, Tingshu Wang
item.content:encoded: About 20 Chinese rescue workers in bright orange operated excavators, shovels and ground-penetrating radar detectors on Sunday in an effort to find hundreds of people missing since a tsunami-like mudslide destroyed China’s main border crossing with Nepal. The Gyirong border crossing separating China's Tibet and Nepal became a grisly emblem of the devastation that followed the collapse of a glacier on the Nepal side of the border on August 26. Reuters and other news agencies visited the land port, which sits in a narrow river gorge, in the first trip organized for foreign media by China's foreign ministry. There was no trace of the five-storey Chinese customs building that had stood at the border before the disaster, video and pictures from the scene showed. The only structure still visible from before the mudslide was a portion of a nearby water tower installation. Workers had placed a Chinese flag at the spot where the border gate, at nearly 20-meters-tall, once stood. Behind hazard signs that read “Danger Area Pass Quickly”, three groups of about 20 rescue and recovery workers dug the earth using shovels while several red excavators stood by on Sunday afternoon. COMPLICATED OPERATION Rescue workers have divided the search area into seven zones, officials told Reuters. They have completed searches in four of them, with three remaining. The mudslide has killed more than 1,300 people on both sides of the border, with more than 5,000 missing. On Saturday, emergency crews in Nepal rescued a [USN:L4N44X01J TEXT:"Chinese worker"] who had been in a tunnel linked to a hydropower station. On China's side of the border, 31 people had been confirmed dead while 531 others were still classified as missing as of Friday. Among those still unaccounted for are 261 foreigners from 23 countries, Chinese officials have said. Gyirong County sits at an average altitude of more than 4,000 meters, though the port itself lies lower, at around 1,800 meters. The risk of landslides, poor weather and deep mud has further complicated rescue and recovery efforts. The only land route into Gyirong was restored by Wednesday morning, allowing China to bring in heavy equipment to aid recovery and eventual rebuilding. State media has shown workers restoring power to the area by sinking temporary electric poles to reconnect it to the grid. HINDU PILGRIMAGE SITE Gyirong has emerged as the main border crossing for travelers and trade between Nepal and Tibet over the past decade, after a 2015 earthquake in Nepal badly damaged an alternative crossing farther east. The port was shut down between July last year and January because of an earlier glacial flood. In addition to a shipment point to Nepal for Chinese goods, including electric cars, it had also become a crossing point for thousands of Hindu pilgrims in recent years. Many Hindus travel through Nepal to Mount Kailash, a high-altitude site in Tibet revered by Hindus and Buddhists. Hindus believe it to be the eternal home of Lord Shiva and his wife Parvati. Many of the foreign nationals still missing in Tibet were pilgrims with extended families in India, diplomats in Beijing have said. There are 49 Indian citizens among the missing.

item.title: All Blacks suffer another injury setback
item.description: New Zealand will have to do without another of their starters for next weekend’s final match against South Africa after Luke Jacobson was added to the injury list following Saturday’s defeat in the third test.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: New Zealand will have to do without another of their starters for next weekend’s final match against South Africa after Luke Jacobson was added to the injury list following Saturday’s defeat in the third test. Jacobson has an elbow injury and joins captain Ardie Savea and centre Quinn Tupaea, who will miss out on the trip to Baltimore in the United States for the last international of the All Blacks' South Africa tour. It will be played next Saturday. Savea dislocated a shoulder in the first half of Saturday’s 29-24 defeat to the Springboks at Soccer City in a major blow to Kiwi hopes while centre Tupaea sustained a knee ligament tear, All Blacks officials said. South Africa, who lead the series 2-1, head to the U.S. without star winger Cheslin Kolbe, who broke his jaw in Saturday’s clash.

item.title: Germany plans anti-sabotage shield after airport drone attack
item.description: Germany is planning a broad package of measures to strengthen its defences against drone attacks, cyber intrusions and other forms of Russian sabotage after a failed airport drone attack last month, an interior ministry spokesperson said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Germany is planning a broad package of measures to strengthen its defences against drone attacks, cyber intrusions and other forms of Russian sabotage after a [USN:L8N44U0IR TEXT:"failed airport drone attack"] last month, an interior ministry spokesperson said on Sunday. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt told the Bild am Sonntag newspaper, which first reported the plans, that Russia's hybrid attacks had become a part of daily reality. "These attacks will increase, but we can defend and protect ourselves," Dobrindt was quoted as saying. Russia has long rejected allegations it is carrying out operations in Western Europe and has denied involvement in the German airport attack, with Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov saying the accusations were [USN:L1N44Y02K TEXT:""the start of a real war""], according to state news agency TASS. According to the ministry spokesperson, police mobile drone defence capabilities would be expanded under the plan, with rapidly deployable counter-drone units stationed in cities to protect the airspace above critical transport hubs and government districts. Companies operating critical infrastructure, such as power utilities and defence manufacturers, would be granted the legal authority to not merely detect drones but also actively fend them off. A national protective shield, or "cyberdome", would be established, involving a network of digital sensors designed to detect and intercept attempted hacking attacks. The government also intends to expand the use of AI-supported technologies, biometric facial recognition and video surveillance, for example at railway stations, to identify suspected attackers preparing acts of sabotage.

item.title: MLB roundup: Kyle Schwarber homers, Phillies beat East-leading Braves
item.description: Zack Wheeler worked six strong innings and Kyle Schwarber hit his major league-leading 41st homer as the Philadelphia Phillies topped the visiting Atlanta Braves 4-2 on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Zack Wheeler worked six strong innings and Kyle Schwarber hit his major league-leading 41st homer as the Philadelphia Phillies topped the visiting Atlanta Braves 4-2 on Saturday. The Phillies evened the four-game series at one win apiece and moved within four games of the first-place Braves in the National League East. Schwarber had two hits for Philadelphia, as did Bryce Harper, Derek Hill and Luis Arraez. Wheeler (12-5) struck out nine while allowing one run and three hits. Atlanta, which had won nine of its last 11, managed only five hits, including solo homers from Ronald Acuna Jr. and Austin Riley. Braves starter Martin Perez (8-9) gave up four runs and seven hits in 3 2/3 innings. Dodgers 6, Nationals 5 Tommy Edman hit a go-ahead three-run home run in the seventh inning as Los Angeles rallied to beat visiting Washington. Teoscar Hernandez had an RBI single in the first inning as the Dodgers earned their third victory in three days without Shohei Ohtani. Edman was occupying Ohtani's leadoff spot, while Hernandez replaced Ohtani as designated hitter. Dodgers right-hander Tyler Glasnow tied a season high by allowing four runs over six-plus innings but didn't factor into the decision. Left-hander Alex Vesia (2-1) pitched one inning to earn the win and Tanner Scott pitched the ninth for his 21st save. Cubs 6, Marlins 5 Ian Happ drove in two runs, and Michael Conforto slugged a solo homer as Chicago defeated host Miami. The Cubs will go for a three-game sweep of the Marlins on Sunday. Ryan Zeferjahn got the final five outs without allowing a run to earn his first save with the Cubs and fifth of the season. Conforto's homer was the major league-leading 200th of the season for the Cubs. Griffin Conine led Miami with a two-run homer measured at 430 feet in the fifth inning. Kyle Stowers added the longest home run of his career, a 442-foot solo blast, in the seventh. Giants 9, Mets 5 Christian Koss and Rafael Devers both hit two homers to help visiting San Francisco beat New York in the middle game of a three-game series. Anthony Molina (3-0) and five relievers combined on a five-hitter for the Giants, who halted a two-game skid. Devers homered in the first and fifth innings, giving him six in the last six games, while Oslevis Basabe and Grant McCray each homered in the final two innings. Molina allowed just one hit over his five innings. A.J. Ewing hit a two-run homer and Brett Baty had three RBIs for the Mets, whose two-game winning streak ended. Rookie Zac Thornton (3-5) was roughed up for six runs on seven hits in five innings. Red Sox 5, Orioles 0 Sonny Gray pitched seven scoreless innings to earn his major league-leading 17th win as Boston won its third straight against host Baltimore. The Red Sox can sweep the four-game series Sunday. Gray (17-4), who was facing Baltimore for the first time this season, held the Orioles to three hits and three walks while striking out seven. Baltimore finished with five hits, struck out 10 times and collected three doubles. Chris Bassitt (6-5) went 5 2/3 innings and was charged with three runs in the loss. Tigers 6, Guardians 0 Riley Greene had four RBIs in his ninth career multi-homer game, and Framber Valdez (9-10) pitched a season-high-tying seven scoreless innings as visiting Detroit downed Cleveland. All-Star rookie Parker Messick (11-9) had a career-high 12 strikeouts over six innings and allowed three runs on seven hits and two walks for the Guardians, who won both games of a doubleheader in walk-off fashion on Friday. item.title: US carrier Abraham Lincoln departs Thailand after respite visit
item.description: The U.S. aircraft carrier Abraham Lincoln left Thailand on Sunday after a five-day port visit, ending a respite from an extended deployment that included operations in the Middle East, the U.S. Navy said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The U.S. aircraft carrier Abraham Lincoln left Thailand on Sunday after a five-day port visit, ending a respite from an extended deployment that included operations in the Middle East, the U.S. Navy said. “We would like to thank the people of Thailand for their incredible hospitality,” U.S. Navy Captain Dan Keeler, the Abraham Lincoln’s commanding officer, said in a statement. Naval deployments typically last for six to nine months, but during times of conflict that can be extended. The nuclear-powered Lincoln, with roughly 5,000 personnel, was involved in the U.S. [USN:L8N44N1OO TEXT:"naval blockade"] and combat operations in the war with Iran and — according to Democratic lawmakers — set a modern-day record for consecutive days at sea. Accompanied by other U.S. naval vessels, the Lincoln arrived early on Wednesday in Thailand, the United States' only treaty partner in [USN:L1N44M08V TEXT:"mainland Southeast Asia"], during a visit that Thai officials said would last five days. Busloads of sailors and Marines wearing civilian clothes, many smiling and waving, started arriving at a hotel in the resort city of Pattaya, about 150 km (93 miles) southeast of Bangkok, shortly after their ships docked.

item.title: Zverev reaches US Open fourth round with win over Tabilo
item.description: Top seed Alexander Zverev lost his way in the second set but got his game back under control to secure a 6-2 7-6(2) 6-2 victory over Alejandro Tabilo and reach the fourth round of the U.S. Open on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Shrivathsa Sridhar
item.content:encoded: Top seed Alexander Zverev lost his way in the second set but got his game back under control to secure a 6-2 7-6(2) 6-2 victory over Alejandro Tabilo and reach the fourth round of the U.S. Open on Saturday. After spending a gruelling nine hours and 26 minutes on court across back-to-back five-setters against Lorenzo Sonego and Quentin Halys, the last thing the German would have wanted was another long night on Arthur Ashe Stadium. "My coach was quite smart, he said that best-of-five sets doesn't mean that you have to play five sets. I didn't know it until now, that was quite helpful," Zverev joked later. "I'm happy with my level right now, it's going in the right direction and I'm happy to be in the second week. "I didn't practice much yesterday, only an hour, which is very little for me. I'd spent almost 10 hours on court, so I had to find my rhythm somehow. I still think I can play better, but for now I'm happy with how things are going." The 29-year-old, who won his first Grand Slam title at the French Open and finished runner-up at Wimbledon, stormed out of the blocks by breaking 25th seed Tabilo twice before taking the first set with an unreturnable serve to love. Zverev raced to a 4-2 lead in the second set but his level suddenly dropped, allowing world number 28 Tabilo to claim three games in a row and go within touching distance of drawing level in the match. However, the Chilean was unable to press home the advantage and Zverev, after chiding a courtside fan who appeared to be offering coaching advice during the ensuing tiebreak, rediscovered his composure and his best tennis, pulling away to tighten his grip on the match. The writing was on the wall for Tabilo when Zverev raced ahead 5-2 in the third, and the German booked his place in the round of 16 where 21st-seeded Italian Luciano Darderi awaits.

item.title: Les discussions entre Poutine et les émissaires américains ont été "utiles", selon le Kremlin
item.description: Vladimir Poutine a reçu samedi à Moscou les émissaires américains Steve Witkoff et Jared Kushner avec qui le président russe a tenu des discussions "très utiles", selon son conseiller diplomatique.
item.dc:creator: Dmitry Antonov, Gleb Bryanski
item.content:encoded: Vladimir Poutine a reçu samedi à Moscou les émissaires américains Steve Witkoff et Jared Kushner avec qui le président russe a tenu des discussions "très utiles", selon son conseiller diplomatique. Iouri Ouchakov, qui a dit que les émissaires américains avaient "présenté un certain nombre d'idée concernant les moyens de parvenir à un accord", n'a toutefois fait mention d'aucune avancée significative après cet entretien de plus de trois heures. Vladimir Poutine a dit à Steve Witkoff et Jared Kushner que la Russie effectuait de "vrais progrès" sur le champ de bataille et qu'elle était convaincue d'atteindre ses objectifs, a-t-il précisé. Le chef du Kremlin a également souligné la nécessité de s'occuper des "toutes les racines du conflit", a dit Iouri Ouchakov. "Les discussions ont dépassé un simple échange de positions afin de mettre fin à la crise ukrainienne. Des questions économiques et de possibles accords, d'importance et mutuellement avantageux, pour des projets entre la Russie et les Etats-Unis ont été abordées en détails", a indiqué le conseiller de Vladimir Poutine. "Dans l'ensemble, on peut dire que ces négociations sont arrivées à point nommé et qu'elles ont été très utiles pour chaque partie." L'émissaire russe Kirill Dmitriev a écrit sur le réseau social X que le déplacement de ses homologues américains à Moscou avait été "une importante visite pour la paix". Kirill Dmitriev et Iouri Ouchakov ont tous deux assistés aux [USN:L8N44X02W TEXT:"discussions"] entre Vladimir Poutine et les émissaires américains. Un responsable de la Maison blanche a déclaré à Reuters que les discussions avaient été "substantielles" et que les prochaines étapes seraient annoncées dans les semaines à venir. Ni Steve Witkoff ni Jared Kushner n'ont fait de commentaire à l'issue de leur entretien avec Vladimir Poutine. Ils ont quitté Moscou peu après les discussions et doivent rencontrer dimanche à Kyiv le président ukrainien, Volodimir Zelensky.

item.title: Tommy Edman HR lifts Dodgers to comeback win over Nats
item.description: Tommy Edman hit a go-ahead three-run home run in the seventh inning as the Los Angeles Dodgers rallied for a 6-5 victory over the visiting Washington Nationals on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Tommy Edman hit a go-ahead three-run home run in the seventh inning as the Los Angeles Dodgers rallied for a 6-5 victory over the visiting Washington Nationals on Saturday. Teoscar Hernandez had an RBI single in the first inning as the Dodgers (85-57) earned their third victory in three days without Shohei Ohtani, who is out with a sore left knee and sore right biceps. Edman was occupying Ohtani's leadoff spot, while Hernandez replaced Ohtani as designated hitter. Dodgers right-hander Tyler Glasnow tied a season high by allowing four runs over six-plus innings but didn't factor into the decision. Left-hander Alex Vesia (2-1) pitched one inning to earn the win and Tanner Scott pitched the ninth for his 21st save. Right-hander Cade Cavalli rebounded from a rough first inning to allow two runs over six innings, while retiring 16 of the last 17 batters he faced. Dylan Crews and Daylen Lile each had RBI doubles for Washington (67-77), which lost its third consecutive game. The Dodgers got off to a fast start against Cavalli after Freddie Freeman was hit by a pitch with one out in the first inning. Mookie Betts followed with a single and Hernandez singled to left for a 1-0 lead. Hunter Feduccia followed with his own RBI single for a 2-0 advantage. The Nationals pulled within a run in the second inning when CJ Abrams singled, stole second and eventually scored on a sacrifice fly from Jose Tena. A Keibert Ruiz single to right field against his former club scored Brady House and Crews followed with an RBI double for a 3-2 Washington lead in the fourth. The Nationals increased the advantage to 4-2 in the seventh inning. A Crews double knocked Glasnow from the game and Lile followed with a one-out RBI double off Vesia. After Edman's home run off Clayton Beeter (5-5) put the Dodgers up in the seventh, they added a run in the eighth when Alex Call was hit by a pitch with the bases loaded. The Nationals scored in the ninth on a Lile single and had the potential game-tying run at third with the go-ahead run at second before Scott struck out CJ Abrams to end the game. --Field Level Media

item.title: Israeli strikes kill four in southern Lebanon
item.description: Israeli strikes killed four people, including two women, in southern Lebanon on Sunday, the Lebanese health ministry said, as Israel retaliated for what it said were Hezbollah drone attacks within areas occupied by its troops.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Israeli strikes killed four people, including two women, in southern Lebanon on Sunday, the Lebanese health ministry said, as Israel retaliated for what it said were Hezbollah drone attacks within areas occupied by its troops. Despite a [USN:L1N42R04I TEXT:"U.S.-brokered ceasefire with Hezbollah"] agreed in June, the Israeli military is operating in what it has declared as a security zone in southern Lebanon. Lebanon’s health ministry said that two men were killed in a town on the edge of the zone occupied by Israeli troops, while the two women were killed in Arab Salim, which sits well north of the occupied area. The Israeli military had issued an online evacuation warning at 6 a.m. local (0300 GMT) for areas near a building in Arab Salim that it said it would strike because it was being used by Hezbollah. Two girls were among six others injured in that strike. Lebanese President Joseph Aoun's office called Sunday's strikes, which it said destroyed a hospital and damaged a finance ministry building, "a dangerous escalation" that targeted "purely civilian administrations and health centres". "President Aoun held the Israeli side fully responsible for this ongoing escalation, calling on the United States and the international community to take immediate action to stop these violations and hold the perpetrators accountable," it said. The Israeli military said its targets included what it described as Hezbollah weapons storage facilities and a command centre inside a building previously used as a hospital. It also said it used precision munitions and aerial surveillance to mitigate civilian harm. Sunday's evacuation warning was only the second issued since the June ceasefire announcement. The first online evacuation order came on August 5 for residents of [USN:L1N4420Q3 TEXT:"Mansouri"], near Tyre, though Israel had already dropped leaflets on the village just a week into the ceasefire, telling residents to leave ahead of strikes. Four people were killed and 23 injured across southern Lebanon on Friday, the health ministry said on Saturday, in Israeli strikes launched without evacuation warnings. The Israeli military said those strikes hit Hezbollah weapons storage facilities. Hezbollah said on Saturday that Israel's continued escalation aimed to pressure the Lebanese government, which has been engaged in direct talks with Israel under U.S. auspices — negotiations that the Iran-backed group has rejected. More than 4,300 people have been killed by Israeli strikes in Lebanon since March 2, when Hezbollah fired at Israel in support of Iran.

item.title: Reds top Brewers after lengthy weather delay

item.content:encoded: Matt McLain's home run in the seventh inning broke a tie and the host Cincinnati Reds defeated the Milwaukee Brewers 5-3 on Saturday night. The game featured a rain delay of almost two-and-a-half hours with two out in the bottom of the fourth. Elly De La Cruz and Tyler Stephenson also homered for the Reds (68-74), who have won three of their last four. William Contreras homered for the Brewers (88-55), who had won three of their previous four. Tony Santillan (3-4) got the win despite giving up a run in his only inning and Emilio Pagan pitched the ninth for his 21st save. He escaped a bases-loaded, one-out jam. Aaron Ashby (13-3), who gave up McLain's home run, was the loser. Cincinnati starter Andrew Abbott gave up two runs (one earned) and three hits in four innings without a walk and fanned five. Brewers starter Dustin May allowed two runs on five hits in 3 2/3 innings, did not walk a batter and struck out five. Both were replaced after the delay. McLain homered leading off the bottom of the seventh. He lined Ashby's 1-1 sinker to the opposite field and into the right field stands for his 15th home run. Eugenio Suarez scored from second on Grant Anderson's wild pitch in the eighth to make it 5-3. Jackson Chourio's bases-loaded sacrifice fly in the seventh had tied it 3-3 for the Brewers. Stephenson's towering homer leading off the sixth gave Cincinnati a 3-2 lead. He powered JoJo Romero's 3-1 sinker deep into the left field stands for his 15th homer. Jose Trevino's run-scoring single in the fourth tied the contest 2-2 for the Reds just after the restart following the rain delay. Luis Lara's RBI groundout in the third put Milwaukee up 2-1. De La Cruz's 22nd home run in the bottom of the first tied the game 1-1 for the Reds.
